quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it. Drivers in the lane next to the broken line may pass. Drivers in the lane next to the solid line may not.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass first. Once the intersection is clear and the light lets you turn, you can complete your turn.

questions.question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming toward them from the opposite direction. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: Who do drivers have to obey?

options.text: Other drivers whose cars are broken down.

questions.explanation: Drivers must follow the signals and instructions of flaggers. They direct traffic to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass even if it is dangerous.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions.
You can pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you of a winding road. Slow down and be ready to turn.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your car and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles with trailers may not see you behind them. Stay farther back from these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so keep extra distance to see around them.

questions.question: When can you drive at the maximum posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive in perfect conditions. Drive at a safe speed for the traffic around you, up to the maximum limit. Always drive at a speed that is safe for weather, road, and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Press hard on the gas pedal.

questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look straight out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they cannot show the area directly behind your car. Back up slowly.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way alcohol affects driving.
The same way amphetamines affect driving.
The same way anger affects driving.
The same way driving with teenagers affects driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way alcohol affects driving.
questions.explanation: Tiredness impairs your driving the same way alcohol does. Being awake for 18 hours is like having a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight is like having a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They warn you about dangers ahead. This sign tells you the road is slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: A car with bright headlights is driving toward you at night. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in blind spots. Always look around and watch for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Let the other vehicle pass safely. Do not speed up or slow down. Keep the same speed so they can merge back into your lane safely.

questions.question: Pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections always have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at intersections. A crosswalk exists anywhere two streets meet, whether it is marked or not.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces. They freeze even when the rest of the road is dry. Bridges also thaw out later than other roads.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're coming.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them lots of space.
Speed ahead and pull in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them lots of space.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as possible. Bicyclists have little protection. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: You must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from every window and mirror.

questions.question: What can you do to help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before you stop.
Release the gas pedal and let your car slow down before you brake.

questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. To stop safely, release the gas pedal first. Then press the brake pedal steadily. This turns on your brake lights and slows your vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: When a school bus ahead on your side of the road has its red lights flashing, you must:

options.text: Slow down to no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: A school bus uses flashing red lights and a stop arm when loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm goes back in. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must or must not do. This sign means you cannot turn left.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line in the center of the road means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction you are traveling.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road ahead.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that pedestrians cross the road ahead. Drive carefully and watch for people who may be crossing.

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout:

options.text: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
Apply the brakes hard and fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, take your foot off the gas pedal. Let your car slow down on its own. Only use the brakes lightly once the car has slowed a lot.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are coming to a T intersection.
The road you are on meets a divided highway.
You are driving over a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road you are on meets a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or barrier.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under any railroad gate or barrier.
questions.explanation: Do not drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You can only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.
Traffic on that street flows to the right.
Traffic on that street flows to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street flows to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic flows to the left if there is no sign blocking the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic flows to the right.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is about to end.

questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means the protected turn is ending. Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic. The green arrow is changing to yellow.

questions.question: Your speed does not affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake.
questions.explanation: Higher speed means longer stopping distance. You must stay far behind the vehicle in front of you, especially in fast traffic.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop and then proceed when the signal changes to green or a green arrow appears.
A driver may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop and then proceed when the signal changes to green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a full stop. Do not move until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: When you drive through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at construction or unusual sights. This causes traffic congestion.

questions.question: Drivers must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: You must always stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road from any direction. Be careful around children.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before crossing tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.
